description: March C- memory BIST engine: one address-cell operation per beat over an 8-cell shadow array with ascending and descending elements, mismatch counting, first-failing-address capture and a done/refuse contract
hardware_advantage: A March C- sweep needs 80 address-cell operations and every one of them is read-compare-write against a known pattern, so the fabric runs the whole test at one operation per cycle with a 64-bit cell array in registers: the compare is an 8-bit XOR reduction and the only arithmetic left is saturating counters, which is what lets the BIST engine sit beside a BRAM and test it in place
provenance: original source authored in this workspace; no third-party RTL imported
qualification: engineering candidate; not certified production or side-channel protection
